title: NSCLC Radiogenomics
summary:
Radiogenomics needs the same patients measured both ways, and almost no public resource provides it. This collection does: 211 patients imaged with thin-section CT and whole-body PET/CT before surgical excision, with a subset carrying matched microarray expression data deposited separately in the Gene Expression Omnibus.
The link between the two is recorded in the collection description as prose, not as a structured cross-reference, which is why the pairing is easy to miss. We extract that accession automatically and surface it here. Everything is openly downloadable with no account.
one_liner: 211 non-small cell lung cancers with pre-surgical CT and PET/CT, semantic annotations, segmentations and matched gene expression - a genuinely paired imaging-genomics cohort, fully open, and described only in prose.

useful_for.question: Do quantitative CT or PET features predict gene expression programs in lung adenocarcinoma?
useful_for.rationale: This is the defining radiogenomics question and it needs paired data on the same patients, which this collection provides for the subset with matched microarrays. Imaging is available for all 211.
useful_for.statistical_note: The matched-expression subset described in the collection is around 26 patients, which supports hypothesis generation and feature-level correlation but not a validated predictive model. Confirm the exact overlap before designing.

useful_for.question: How reproducible are radiomic features across CT and PET acquisitions of the same tumor?
useful_for.rationale: Both modalities were acquired for the same patients pre-surgically, so feature stability across modality and acquisition can be assessed directly - a prerequisite for any radiomics claim and rarely testable.
useful_for.statistical_note: Reproducibility is estimable at this sample size; report intraclass correlation.

useful_for.question: Can models trained on this cohort's segmentations generalize to other lung imaging collections in the same repository?
useful_for.rationale: Expert segmentations and semantic annotations are provided, and the Imaging Data Commons holds several other lung collections that can serve as external validation within one access framework.

limitations.statement: The matched imaging-and-expression subset is a small fraction of the 211 imaged patients - the collection describes roughly 26 cases with microarray data. The cohort is imaging-rich and genomics-poor.
limitations.mitigation: Treat radiogenomic analyses as hypothesis-generating and validate elsewhere. Use the full 211 for imaging-only questions.
